subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures stay in the accepted-then-async run path with a visible terminal startup-failure state, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight sandbox startup before returning `accepted`?
rationale: The choice affects the public `sessions_spawn` contract, lifecycle phase vocabulary, gateway wait behavior, and session/registry state rather than a local Docker error string only.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` accepting the run, but emit/log a typed startup failure that updates session and subagent state when Docker startup fails.

options.title: Preflight before accepted
options.body: Start or validate the sandbox before returning `accepted`, trading clearer immediate failure for extra latency and a stricter spawn contract.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle tracker
options.body: Keep this issue as the sandbox proof case while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776 decides the broader first-progress/startup-failed lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` accepting the run, but emit/log a typed startup failure that updates session and subagent state when Docker startup fails.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest cross-surface work on subagent spawn, terminal outcomes, and gateway session lifecycle paths.
